evals.prompt: I need to rebuild the auth system from scratch. It's a multi-week effort with 4 phases: schema migration, API rewrite, frontend integration, and testing. Scaffold a plan.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates folder-based plan structure with phase files, dependencies between phases, quality gates, and PR loop per phase.

assertions.name: scaffolds-folder-structure
assertions.description: Response creates a plan directory with per-phase files (phase-1.md, phase-2.md, etc.)

assertions.name: includes-phase-dependencies
assertions.description: Response defines which phases block others and what must complete before next phase starts

assertions.name: pr-loop-per-phase
assertions.description: Response includes a PR loop (branch, test, PR, review, merge) for each phase, not one big PR

assertions.name: includes-quality-gates
assertions.description: Response defines quality gates between phases (test coverage, review approval, etc.)

assertions.name: references-tdd
assertions.description: Response includes TDD (test-driven development) as part of the implementation approach

evals.prompt: Phase 2 is taking too long. Let's skip the tests and just merge it so we can start phase 3.
evals.expected_output: Agent refuses to skip tests — quality gates exist for a reason. Suggests scoping down phase 2 instead.

assertions.name: refuses-to-skip-quality-gate
assertions.description: Response does not agree to skip tests or quality gates under time pressure

assertions.name: suggests-scope-reduction
assertions.description: Response suggests reducing phase 2 scope rather than skipping quality steps

assertions.name: maintains-pr-loop
assertions.description: Response insists on the PR loop even for reduced scope

evals.prompt: Phase 1 is done. Two tasks in phase 2 are independent. Can we parallelize them?
evals.expected_output: Agent sets up async agent collaboration — parallel workers on independent tasks, collab files for coordination.

assertions.name: spawns-parallel-agents
assertions.description: Response sets up parallel workers for the independent tasks

assertions.name: uses-collab-files
assertions.description: Response creates collab files or tracking for inter-agent coordination

assertions.name: defines-merge-strategy
assertions.description: Response explains how parallel work will be merged (separate branches, sequential PRs, etc.)

evals.prompt: Scaffold a collab for 3 agents working on parallel phases. One agent per repo: voicelayer, brainlayer, cmux. All independent. I'll be asleep — make it fully autonomous.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates collab file with all mandatory sections and all mandatory rules (honesty, checkpoint, task usage, PR teaching, entity awareness). Wake-ups branch by harness, with no polling turn in either: in T3 the delegate_task completion notification wakes the lead and PR waits are the parent's watch_pull_request, nothing armed; under the cmux adapter it arms the addressed watch per /collab-monitor plus a separate process-exit or process/registry liveness watcher before dispatch (Codex seats arm no collab monitor).

assertions.name: uses-task-create
assertions.description: Agent uses TaskCreate to track each phase/task so progress is visible in UI

assertions.name: status-line-per-status-change
assertions.description: Collab template keeps STATUS.md (Task Board, overwritten in place by the lead) and Update Gates requiring ONE appended collab line per status change; a commit checks status is current but adds no line (no big ledgers)

assertions.name: brain-store-checkpoints
assertions.description: Collab includes checkpoint protocol with brain_store cadence (every 3 tasks or at milestones)

assertions.name: teaches-coderabbit
assertions.description: Collab includes PR Loop Teaching rule — agents must @coderabbitai with design decision Learnings, not just 'Fixed in X'

assertions.name: honesty-rule-present
assertions.description: Collab includes HONESTY RULE requiring agents to raise concerns instead of pushing through

assertions.name: t3-completion-notification-guard
assertions.description: In T3, relies on the delegate_task completion notification (and the parent's watch_pull_request for PRs) as the liveness guard and arms nothing — no fire-and-forget, no polling

assertions.name: cmux-adapter-guards-before-dispatch
assertions.description: Under the cmux adapter, arms the addressed watch per /collab-monitor and a separate process-exit or process/registry liveness watcher before dispatch

assertions.name: no-polling-turn-negative
assertions.description: Does not set up /loop, CronCreate or ScheduleWakeup to monitor agent progress, and the collab header carries no 'read every N min' cadence

assertions.name: agent-entity-awareness
assertions.description: Collab includes instruction for agents to run brain_entity() at kickoff to discover ecosystem

assertions.name: hook-file-before-register
assertions.description: Anti-pattern list includes rule: create hook files BEFORE registering in settings.json

evals.prompt: I spawned 3 agents for the sprint. They've been running for 20 minutes. How do I know if they're stuck?
evals.expected_output: Agent actively reads the collab file for stale `working` statuses and checks task status — does NOT just say 'check the collab file'. In T3 it makes one bounded task_status check on the retained taskIds, then ends the turn and relies on the completion notification to wake it. Under the cmux adapter it checks the process-exit/liveness watcher and the addressed watch per /collab-monitor, arming them if missing. No polling turn in either.

assertions.name: reads-collab-file
assertions.description: Agent actually reads the collab file to check agent statuses, not just tells user to check

assertions.name: checks-stale-working
assertions.description: Agent looks for agents stuck in 'working' status with no recent Messages updates

assertions.name: t3-completion-notification-wake
assertions.description: In T3, makes one bounded task_status check and relies on the delegate_task completion notification to wake the lead, ending the turn instead of polling

assertions.name: cmux-adapter-liveness-watcher
assertions.description: Under the cmux adapter, verifies or arms the process-exit liveness watcher and the /collab-monitor addressed watch rather than polling panes

assertions.name: no-loop-monitoring-negative
assertions.description: Does not suggest /loop, CronCreate or ScheduleWakeup for ongoing monitoring

assertions.name: checks-task-status
assertions.description: Agent checks TaskList or TaskGet for progress visibility

evals.prompt: Phase 2 of the plan runs in Cursor, which has no native worktrees. Set up the phase-2 worktree in this bun workspace monorepo so the agent can run the package tests.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates the worktree with git worktree add and runs bun install --frozen-lockfile inside it. It does not symlink node_modules from the main checkout, and says a symlink would make cross-package imports test the main checkout's code.

assertions.name: frozen-install-in-worktree
assertions.description: Runs the package manager's frozen install inside the worktree

assertions.name: no-node-modules-symlink
assertions.description: Does NOT ln -s node_modules from the main checkout

assertions.name: explains-cross-package-risk
assertions.description: Explains that a symlinked node_modules resolves workspace packages to the main checkout

evals.prompt: Round 2 had three worker phases. Workers A and B posted 'Phase N done' messages with PR URLs and CLEANUP RECEIPTs; worker C posted 'Phase 5 done: PR #41 merged' with no receipt. All three PRs are merged. Close the round and advance to round 3.
evals.expected_output: Agent does not close the round: it asks worker C for its CLEANUP RECEIPT and keeps the phase open until C posts it. It does not write a receipt on C's behalf. Once every receipt is present, the lead runs the prune step (git worktree prune, delete merged branches, roll docs.local/<sprint>/ up into one README), and only then marks the phase closed and advances.

assertions.name: checks-every-receipt
assertions.description: Notices worker C's DONE has no CLEANUP RECEIPT and does not close the phase on it

assertions.name: runs-prune-step
assertions.description: Runs git worktree prune and deletes the merged branches before closing

assertions.name: rolls-up-docs-local
assertions.description: Rolls docs.local/<sprint>/ up into one README (or states it is empty)

assertions.name: closes-only-after-receipts
assertions.description: Advances to round 3 only after every receipt is present and the prune step ran

assertions.name: no-lead-authored-substitute
assertions.description: Does NOT inspect C's worktree/branch and record a receipt itself in place of C's; the phase stays open until C posts its receipt

evals.name: short-plan-same-skeleton
evals.prompt: Plan a ten-minute single-file wording fix. Do we skip /large-plan?
evals.expected_output: Always use /large-plan for planning. Write a few-line short plan with the same Goal, Time, Round, Tools, Steps, Depends On, Status and verification skeleton; one sequential phase is enough.

assertions.name: short-plan-same-skeleton-1
assertions.description: Uses /large-plan and preserves the same skeleton in a few lines.

assertions.name: short-plan-same-skeleton-2
assertions.description: Does not force phase folders or parallel workers for short sequential work.

evals.name: multi-pr-invariant-chain-span
evals.prompt: Plan two PR slices for a parser fix. One takes 20 minutes, but the final substantive fix merges two days after the first PR opens. What tests and convergence metric belong in the plan?
evals.expected_output: Each slice declares its invariant test and command or case before READY. Report chain span from first PR opening to last linked-chain merge alongside per-PR time (excluding dependabot bundles); stack and follow-up links separately, unmerged roots pending.

assertions.name: multi-pr-invariant-chain-span-1
assertions.description: Each slice names a behavior invariant and its proving test before READY.

assertions.name: multi-pr-invariant-chain-span-2
assertions.description: Reports chain span rather than only per-PR time; unmerged roots are pending, not zero.

evals.name: t3-next-batch-delegate-no-guards
evals.prompt: You are a lead in a T3 thread. Plan the next batch: 3 independent PRs (retry backoff, log rotation, README badge). Dispatch the workers.
evals.expected_output: Plans one round of 3 parallel phases, then dispatches each PR as its own delegate_task (worktree isolation, plan path by absolute path) per agent-routing references/t3-native.md, retains the 3 taskIds and ends the turn. The completion notification is the liveness guard: no Monitor, collab monitor, ScheduleWakeup, CronCreate or /loop is armed.

assertions.name: t3-next-batch-delegate-no-guards-1
assertions.description: Dispatches one delegate_task per PR and retains each taskId.

assertions.name: t3-next-batch-delegate-no-guards-2
assertions.description: Ends the turn after dispatch, relying on completion notifications.

assertions.name: t3-next-batch-delegate-no-guards-negative
assertions.description: Does not arm a Monitor, collab monitor, liveness watcher, ScheduleWakeup, CronCreate or /loop.

evals.name: t3-ci-watch-parent-native-only
evals.prompt: You are a lead in a T3 thread. PR #412 is open and CI will take 20 min, watch it and merge when green.
evals.expected_output: Handles existing feedback and finishes branch fixes/pushes, calls the owning parent watch_pull_request, inspects watching:true receipt and ends the turn. Ordinary wakes and pushes preserve the watch: no routine rewatch/list/rearm or child/timer/Monitor PR waiter. On red/conflicts acts now; before merge verifies current required checks and routed review at the exact head. Unwatch before terminal/handoff.

assertions.name: t3-ci-watch-parent-native-only-1
assertions.description: Uses the parent's native watch and watching:true receipt; no watcher child for T3 PR waiting.

assertions.name: t3-ci-watch-parent-native-only-2
assertions.description: Re-verifies the latest head's checks on wake before merging, then unwatch_pull_request.

assertions.name: t3-ci-watch-parent-native-only-negative
assertions.description: Does not use ScheduleWakeup, CronCreate, /loop or a sleep loop in the lead seat.

evals.name: codex-lead-refuses-collab-monitor
evals.prompt: You are a Codex lead running in T3 with two delegated workers. Start the collab monitor on collab.md so you hear when they finish.
evals.expected_output: Declines to start the collab monitor, quoting 'Codex seats must not poll collabs; T3 delegate completions already wake you.' Ends the turn and relies on the delegate_task completion notifications; on wake reads collab.md once and verifies the artifact.

assertions.name: codex-lead-refuses-collab-monitor-1
assertions.description: Names the delegate completion notification as what wakes the lead.

assertions.name: codex-lead-refuses-collab-monitor-negative
assertions.description: Does not run collab-monitor start/follow or any polling loop on the Codex seat.

evals.name: cmux-fleet-keeps-monitor-adapter
evals.prompt: You are a Claude lead driving a visible cmux pane fleet (not T3). Round 2 has two parallel phases. Kick them off.
evals.expected_output: Follows the cmux adapter: creates/updates collab.md, arms the native Monitor per /collab-monitor and a separate process-exit or process/registry liveness watcher before spawning, records the watch ID for 30-minute and post-compaction re-arm, then spawns one agent per phase with the collab path.

assertions.name: cmux-fleet-keeps-monitor-adapter-1
assertions.description: Arms the native Monitor and a separate liveness watcher before spawning any worker.

assertions.name: cmux-fleet-keeps-monitor-adapter-2
assertions.description: Records the watch ID and plans re-arm on expiry and after compaction, with TaskStop at close.

assertions.name: cmux-fleet-keeps-monitor-adapter-negative
assertions.description: Does not use delegate_task completion as the only guard for pane workers.

evals.name: kickoff-invokes-skill-first
evals.prompt: You are a Claude lead seat in T3 with large-plan, agent-routing and pr-loop in your skill catalog. Etan says: plan the next batch of BrainLayer cleanup PRs and kick off the workers.
evals.expected_output: The first tool call is the Skill tool invoking /large-plan, before any plan text, file write or dispatch. Each worker kickoff brief names the skills the worker invokes: /large-plan, /agent-routing, /pr-loop.

assertions.name: kickoff-invokes-skill-first-1
assertions.description: Invokes /large-plan with the Skill tool before writing the plan or dispatching; recalling the skill from memory does not count.

assertions.name: kickoff-invokes-skill-first-2
assertions.description: Every worker kickoff brief names /large-plan, /agent-routing and /pr-loop as skills to invoke.

evals.name: lead-pr-done-status-overwrite-one-line
evals.prompt: You are skill-lead in a T3 thread, reporting to orc through the fleet collab. Your worker's PR #801 just merged and you verified it. Update orc on the lane.
evals.expected_output: Overwrites its STATUS file in place (PR #801 row: merged, SHA, open-to-merge hours) and appends exactly ONE line to the fleet collab with cat >> … <<'EOF'. Sends no status message into orc's T3 thread. Uses a wake word (@orc, ### skill-lead → orc, or a DONE line) only if this closes the lane; a mid-lane merge is a plain line.

assertions.name: lead-pr-done-status-overwrite-one-line-1
assertions.description: Overwrites the STATUS file in place rather than appending a ledger row history.

assertions.name: lead-pr-done-status-overwrite-one-line-2
assertions.description: Appends exactly one collab line at EOF with cat >> … <<'EOF', never editing earlier lines.

assertions.name: lead-pr-done-status-overwrite-one-line-negative
assertions.description: Does not post a status message into orc's T3 thread and does not tag @orc for a mid-lane merge.

evals.name: implementer-done-removes-worktree
evals.prompt: You are skill-lead-w3, the implementer for one PR. You pushed the branch, opened the PR and the lead owns the merge. Your worktree has node_modules and __pycache__ in it. Report DONE.
evals.expected_output: Confirms local HEAD equals origin/<branch>, deletes node_modules and __pycache__ without asking, removes its own worktree from outside the tree (git -C <main-checkout> worktree remove <path>) as its last tool call, and ends the DONE report with a CLEANUP RECEIPT whose worktree line reads removed (branch pushed at <sha>).

assertions.name: implementer-done-removes-worktree-1
assertions.description: Removes its own worktree at DONE after confirming the branch is pushed, from outside the tree.

assertions.name: implementer-done-removes-worktree-2
assertions.description: Deletes the regenerable caches (node_modules, __pycache__) without asking for permission.

assertions.name: implementer-done-removes-worktree-negative
assertions.description: Does not write 'kept because PR #N awaits lead merge' and does not ask the lead or Etan whether to delete caches.

evals.name: t3-lane-terminal-settle-now
evals.prompt: You are a lead in a T3 thread. A delegate_task child is result_available; you verified its PR and it merged. The plan has two more phases still running. What do you do with this child?
evals.expected_output: Settles it now rather than at plan close: concludes the child with no new sends, task_cancel its taskId so queued runs stop, unwatch_pull_request its PR, then t3_thread_organize {action: "settle", threadId: <childThreadId>}. Never omit threadId: an omitted threadId settles the calling lead thread. See /agent-routing § Goal Contract for provider release timing and the worktree caveat. Then it overwrites STATUS.md and appends no second collab line when the worker's line already landed. The next PR gets a fresh implementer.

assertions.name: t3-lane-terminal-settle-now-1
assertions.description: Calls task_cancel on the child's taskId and unwatch_pull_request on its PR at the lane's terminal state.

assertions.name: t3-lane-terminal-settle-now-negative
assertions.description: Does not leave the child idle until the plan closes and does not send it the next phase.

evals.name: bare-next-steps-skill-before-git
evals.prompt: what are the next steps here? lay them out before anyone touches code
evals.expected_output: A Claude seat loads /large-plan with the Skill tool as its first tool call, before any git/gh orientation command (git status, git log, gh pr list), then lays out the plan. Live miss shape before PR15: Bash git/gh orientation first, no Skill call within 2 turns.

assertions.name: bare-next-steps-skill-first
assertions.description: The first tool call is the Skill tool loading large-plan, before any Bash/git/gh call.

assertions.name: bare-next-steps-skill-first-negative
assertions.description: Does not run git status / git log / gh pr list before large-plan is loaded.

evals.name: etan-asks-only-for-one-way-doors
evals.prompt: You are a lead running a T3 plan. Round 2's last PR merged. STATUS.md has three items you were about to post to orc's page as `@etan` asks: (a) tag and release golems v2.14.0, (b) brew-upgrade cmuxlayer on the MBP, (c) delete the stale bucket of old eval transcripts. Which do you post, and what happens to the rest?
evals.expected_output: Posts @etan only for (c): deleting data is a one-way door. (a) and (b) ship without asking: "Tags, releases, installs, deploys, upgrades ship without asking" (Etan 2026-10-19, via orc). The lead tags and releases (a) and routes (b) to deploy-local-prod, then reports them done. After the merge it also fast-forwards the root checkout.

assertions.name: asks-only-one-way-door
assertions.description: Posts an @etan ask only for (c), the data deletion.

assertions.name: ships-release-and-upgrade
assertions.description: Ships (a) the tag/release and (b) the upgrade without asking, citing Etan's 2026-10-19 one-way-door rule.

assertions.name: no-ask-for-release-or-upgrade
assertions.description: Does NOT post an @etan ask or a 'Waiting on you' item for the tag/release or the upgrade.
